result:
I found 11 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behaviour didn't match their docstring or the module-wide rules, and fixed all of them. A check script now finds 0 mismatches across all 150 rules.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 03, 107 | The cap only applied when the discount was over 60,000 won, so a discount between 30,001 and 60,000 won was never capped | Always cap the discount |
| 139 | The cap was applied to the price before the percentage, not to the discount (module docstring says the discount is capped) | Calculate the discount, then cap it |
| 29, 48 | Same problem in marginal rules: the cap was applied to the amount above the threshold before the percentage | Calculate the discount, then cap it |
| 19, 66 | Marked "whole" but calculated as marginal (only units above the threshold) | Switched to whole: `base * pct // 100` |
| 68 | Marked "marginal" but calculated as whole | Switched to marginal: `(qty - 20) * unit * pct // 100` |
| 54 | Used `round(...)`, but discounts must be floored to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 59, 71 | Used `qty > threshold`, so the discount didn't apply at exactly the threshold quantity ("N+ units") | Changed to `>=` |

**How I checked:** a script (`/tmp/chk/check.py`) reads each docstring to get the type, percentage, threshold and cap, and works out the expected amount. It compares that with the actual return value for quantities around each threshold and a range of unit prices, and also checks that negative inputs raise `ValueError`. The 11 rules above were the only ones that failed before the fix. Some other rules are written differently, such as `if not qty < 50:` or `if disc > 30000: disc = 30000`, but they give the same results, so I left them unchanged. `RULES` and `quote()` still load and work. The original file is backed up at `/tmp/chk/pricebook.orig.py`.

STATUS: DONE
